_trigger: THE SUBJECT OF THIS SCENARIO. Loading a save calls [UNIVERSE populateNormalSpace] (PlayerEntityLoadSave.m:777), which fires the systemWillPopulate WORLD-SCRIPT EVENT (Universe.m:1732-1737). oolite-cloaking-device-mission.js:47-103 handles it: in galaxy 5 (galaxyNumber === 4) with missionVariables.cloak unset it does `missionVariables.cloakcounter++` (:62) and, once the counter exceeds 6 with no asp-cloaked present, registers the ambush populator (:71-89) which spawns the cloaked Asp and two escorts.
_counter: THE FALSIFIABLE CORE. The fixture holds 6 ON DISK; the running engine reads 7. A value the deserialiser merely COPIED would read 6, so file+1 is positive proof the mission script's own code ran. expected_counter_in_file is pinned because 6 is exactly the value that makes the incremented counter exceed the script's `> 6` threshold - a different fixture value would change whether the ambush is spawned at all.
_side_effects: The two other consequences of the SAME `if` block, so the counter cannot be the only witness. The populator key is created by that block's system.setPopulator() call and by nothing else; the role counts are literals in the block's callback (1 asp-cloaked, 2 asp-pirate).
_handlers: systemWillPopulate must STILL be a live function on the script object: startUp deletes it when missionVariables.cloak is already set (oolite-cloaking-device-mission.js:38-45), and a script with no handler cannot have been the thing that fired.
_mission_variables: The measured POST-trigger set. Note cloakcounter is 7 here, not the file's 6: this dict is read out of the running engine after the event. A fresh game's is EMPTY.
_control: The differential control arm: the IDENTICAL scenario with a different checklist save. Constrictor.oolite-save is in galaxy 1, so the trigger's own `galaxyNumber === 4` guard fails - the mission script is LOADED but its handler does nothing. That is sharper than a dead run: it proves the assertions measure the TRIGGER FIRING and not merely 'a game with a save in it'.
_fresh: The second control arm: a game launched with NO -load at all. The world scripts are not built, so the mission script itself is absent.
